episode_title: Mastering the Job Search in 2024 with Erika Klics, Job Search Strategist

real_qa.q: What is the most effective job search strategy in 2024 for directors and VPs?
real_qa.r: Job searching in 2024 requires a lot more thought, strategy, outreach, and output to really get the job search moving because the market is really unsettled. Most people who had received previous jobs through LinkedIn emails or inbound offers are now finding that approach no longer works for most candidates. The most effective current approach involves taking a step back to reflect on what you actually want, then using networking-based hiring and cold outreach strategies to target the right companies and hiring teams directly.

real_qa.q: How should job candidates approach resume writing to stand out in 2024?
real_qa.r: Rather than simply pulling out an old resume and tacking recent bullets onto it, candidates should conduct an experience inventory by doing a brain dump of all their experience and then working backwards to reflect on what they actually want and what they've actually done. The key is to take a step back and think about your experience through a wider, personally fruitful lens beyond just your current company's context. Then the resume story changes entirely—same job, same dates, but totally different narrative focused on what you actually want to do next.

real_qa.q: Why do job descriptions with 20-30 bullet points often fail to describe real roles?
real_qa.r: Job descriptions right now are not very well written, with many containing 20 or 30 bullets about what a company wants in a person, which doesn't describe a real person. These descriptions are often contradictory—for example, posting entry-level associate positions that require 25 years of experience, or director-level roles that expect tactical execution work with no actual leadership responsibilities. This makes it difficult for candidates to understand what a company truly needs or to present themselves effectively based on job board descriptions.

real_qa.q: How can candidates demonstrate leadership in interviews despite market uncertainty?
real_qa.r: When hiring leaders, companies need leaders to challenge what's happening and ask hard questions. The great interviewers and candidates who do well take ownership of their own leadership in the search by showing up as the leader they will be in the role, rather than clamming up or only asking safe questions. Candidates should come to the interview ready to take a bold stance, positioning themselves as the expert who can solve the company's problems, similar to a consulting or sales approach.

real_qa.q: What percentage of director and VP roles are now filled through referrals versus applications?
real_qa.r: A healthy mix in recruiting a couple of years ago would have been about a third inbound recruiter, outbound, and referrals. Now, at least with the clients Erika works with, the split is about 50-50 between getting jobs through referrals versus applications. Leaders are still getting roles through cold applications, but increasingly more traction and interviews come through referral-based hiring.

real_qa.q: Should job candidates create LinkedIn content to get discovered by recruiters?
real_qa.r: While there's a big push right now to be a content creator on LinkedIn, posting frequently so someone discovers you and wants to hire you, that's not necessarily how hiring works. Hiring has always worked by building a talent pool and bench of potential candidates, but when a role actually opens, it often has nothing to do with the pipeline that was built beforehand. Content creation is a long-tail game that is not a here-and-now solution to job searching.
